key_insight: Deep learning of routine melanoma histopathology added prognostic information beyond AJCC stage, with the combined model achieving a C-index of 0.87 versus 0.80 for stage alone.
clinical_relevance: This prognostic approach could support future risk stratification in early-stage melanoma, but it does not establish treatment benefit or discover new drugs.
method: Automatically extracted relevant patches from primary melanoma whole-slide images.
Trained a patient-level metastatic-risk model using 328 patients and 10-fold cross-validation.
Evaluated independent prognostic value in a population-based nested case-control validation sample.
evidence_signal: Validation included 266 patients sampled from a cohort of more than 5,500; model predictions remained independently prognostic (adjusted OR 1.97, p<0.01), and combining them with AJCC stage improved discrimination versus stage alone (p<0.001).
watch_item: Clinical deployment requires further validation across settings and evidence that model-guided decisions improve outcomes.
paper_title: Deep learning reveals prognostic information beyond AJCC stage in routine histopathology of early-stage melanoma: the population-based D-ESMEL study
